authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The conversion condition for the 2030 convertible notes was met: the stock price exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the required trading days. Holders may therefore convert the notes at their option during the quarter ending December 29, 2026.
The Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.30 per share, payable November 24, 2026 to holders of record on November 10, 2026.
The President of the bakery subsidiary notified the company of his decision to retire. He will stay in the role into the first quarter of 2027 to assist with the leadership transition.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The licensing revenue stream is inferred from the licensing agreements, and its size is not given.
business_model.claim: The company makes money by owning and operating restaurants in the US and Canada, and currently runs 384 across four groups: The Cheesecake Factory (218), North Italia (53), Flower Child (47) and other Fox Restaurant Concepts brands (60). A further 35 The Cheesecake Factory restaurants operate internationally under licensing agreements.
quotes: Our revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and increases in comparable restaurant sales.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and 10-K business descriptions.
business_model.claim: The company also runs a bakery division that makes cheesecakes and other baked goods. They are sold in its own restaurants, to international licensees and to third-party bakery customers.
quotes: Our bakery division operates two facilities that produce quality cheesecakes and other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees and third-party bakery customers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1. The percentages apply to The Cheesecake Factory concept, not the whole company.
business_model.claim: Its customers are restaurant diners at upscale casual prices. The 10-K gives an average check of $31.79 for fiscal 2025. Alcoholic beverages were 11% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales, desserts about 17%, and off-premise orders about 21%.
quotes: The average check for each customer, including beverages and desserts, was approximately $31.79 during fiscal 2025.
During fiscal 2025, alcoholic beverage sales represented 11% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales.

business_model.basis: Stated in the footnotes to the Q3 release's segment table. The Cheesecake Factory and North Italia are presumed to be separate segments, inferred from the 10-K's sales-by-concept discussion.
business_model.claim: Reporting is split by concept. The Other FRC segment covers all Fox Restaurant Concepts brands except Flower Child. The Other segment holds Flower Child, Grand Lux Cafe, the third-party bakery, international and consumer packaged goods businesses, unallocated corporate expenses and gift card costs.
quotes: The Other FRC segment includes all FRC brands except Flower Child.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A. The remainder of fiscal 2025 revenue is not itemised in the extract, so it is not accounted for here.
business_model.claim: Fiscal 2025 revenue was $3,751.8 million. By concept, sales were $2,688.8 million at The Cheesecake Factory, $345.9 million at North Italia, $185.3 million at Flower Child and $355.1 million at Other FRC. The namesake concept is therefore the largest revenue source, and the newer concepts are growing faster.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory sales increased 1.0% to $2,688.8 million for fiscal 2025 compared to $2,661.6 million for fiscal 2024.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the release and the income statement. The causes are management's own attribution, not independently shown.
business_model.claim: Revenue moves with comparable restaurant sales and with new units. Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue was $1,033.4 million against $907.2 million a year earlier, and comparable sales at The Cheesecake Factory rose 15.2%. Management credits menu innovation, the rewards program and social media engagement.
quotes: Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A. The Q3 2026 traffic versus check split is not in the evidence.
business_model.claim: Comparable sales at The Cheesecake Factory come from traffic and average check. Average check depends on menu pricing and mix. In fiscal 2025 comparable sales rose 0.1%, with check up 2.4% and traffic down 2.3%.
quotes: Average check variations are driven by menu price increases and/or changes in menu mix.

business_model.basis: Stated in the release, the 10-Q and the 10-K.
business_model.claim: Unit growth is a core revenue driver. The company opened six restaurants in Q3 fiscal 2026 and continues to expect as many as 26 openings in fiscal 2026. It names new Company-owned restaurants as its top long-term capital allocation priority.
quotes: The Company continues to expect to open as many as 26 new restaurants in fiscal 2026, including as many as five The Cheesecake Factory restaurants, eight North Italia locations, seven Flower Child locations and as many as six FRC restaurants.
Our top long-term capital allocation priority is to develop new Company-owned restaurants, with a focus on opening our concepts in premier locations within new and existing markets.

business_model.basis: Percentages are stated in the Q3 release table. The explanation of the improvement is management's attribution.
business_model.claim: The main cost lines are food and beverage, labor and other restaurant operating costs, which include occupancy. In Q3 fiscal 2026 food and beverage costs were 21.2% of revenues against 21.8% a year earlier, and labor was 34.8% against 35.6%. Management cites better labor productivity and food efficiency.
quotes: Food and beverage costs consist of raw materials and ingredients used in the food and beverage products sold in our restaurants and to our third-party bakery customers.

business_model.claim: Labor is exposed to wage inflation, minimum wage rules and self-insured healthcare costs. The company says its from-scratch menu needs more labor per restaurant than competitors that use processed foods.
quotes: Our labor expenses include significant costs related to our self-insured health, pharmacy and dental benefit plans.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the balance sheet. The operating leverage point is inferred.
business_model.claim: The company leases all of its restaurant locations and spends capital on leasehold improvements and equipment. Construction averages roughly $1,100 to $1,200 per interior square foot. Operating lease assets were 1,548,650 on the balance sheet (table in thousands), so occupancy is a large fixed cost base.
quotes: We currently lease all of our restaurant locations and utilize capital for leasehold improvements and furnishings, fixtures and equipment to build out our restaurant premises.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the income statement and the release. The revaluation mechanism is inferred from the 10-K's description of this line.
business_model.claim: Q3 fiscal 2026 income from operations was 74,873 against 37,269 a year earlier (table in thousands). The quarter included acquisition-related income of (12,889). Net income was $61.3 million while adjusted net income was $52.3 million, so part of the reported profit came from a Fox acquisition-related item.
quotes: The Company recorded a pre-tax net income of $12.9 million related to Fox Restaurant Concepts (“FRC”) acquisition-related items.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the cited items. The seasonal explanation for the decline is not given.
business_model.claim: Gift cards are a working-capital and revenue feature. Gift card liabilities were 176,386 at September 29, 2026 against 212,859 at December 30, 2025 (table in thousands). In fiscal 2025 the company recognized $17.3 million of additional gift card breakage as revenue.
quotes: As a result, in fiscal 2025, we recognized $17.3 million of additional gift card breakage.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement and balance sheet. The 10-K MD&A supports the working-capital point.
business_model.claim: Operations fund expansion. Nine-month operating cash flow was 313,738 against additions to property and equipment shown as (144,238) (table in thousands). Dividends paid were (44,117) and treasury stock purchases were (31,801), also from this cash flow.

competitive_position.claim: The company operates a multi-brand footprint of 384 owned restaurants in the US and Canada, led by The Cheesecake Factory at 218 locations. The others are North Italia at 53, Flower Child at 47 and other Fox Restaurant Concepts brands at 60. A further 35 Cheesecake Factory restaurants are run by international licensees.
quotes: We currently own and operate 384 restaurants throughout the United States and Canada under brands including The Cheesecake Factory® (218 locations), North Italia® (53 locations), Flower Child® (47 locations) and additional brands within our FRC portfolio (60 locations).

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K; these are management's own measures
competitive_position.claim: The company positions The Cheesecake Factory in upscale casual dining, above core casual dining. It cites high sales productivity: about $12.4 million average sales per full-year location and about $1,151 per productive square foot in fiscal 2025.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory restaurants operate in the upscale casual dining segment, which is positioned above core casual dining, with standards that are closer to fine dining.
Average sales per location for The Cheesecake Factory restaurants open for the full year were approximately $12.4 million for fiscal 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the earnings releases and the 10-K
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue was $1,033.4 million versus $907.2 million a year earlier. Comparable sales at The Cheesecake Factory rose 15.2%, after 5.8% in the second quarter and only 0.1% for fiscal 2025. This is the main evidence of competitive strength in the packet.
quotes: Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

competitive_position.basis: stated by management in the release; not verified
competitive_position.claim: Management says Cheesecake Factory comparable sales and traffic meaningfully outperformed the broader casual dining industry. It attributes this to menu innovation, the rewards program and social media engagement. The packet has no independent industry data to check the comparison.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory restaurants led our performance, with comparable sales and traffic meaningfully outperforming the broader casual dining industry.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the income statement and release table
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter cost ratios improved. Food and beverage costs were 21.2% of revenue versus 21.8%, and labor was 34.8% versus 35.6%. Income from operations was 74,873 (table in thousands) versus 37,269. Management credits labor productivity and food efficiency.
quotes: while year-over-year improvements in labor productivity and food efficiency supported strong profitability.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the release and income statement
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter GAAP earnings were flattered by Fox Restaurant Concepts acquisition-related items. These produced $12.9 million of pre-tax net income. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.02 against GAAP diluted EPS of $1.19, so underlying earnings were lower than reported.
quotes: The Company recorded a pre-tax net income of $12.9 million related to Fox Restaurant Concepts (“FRC”) acquisition-related items.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the release and the 10-K
competitive_position.claim: Growth runs through new units. The company expects as many as 26 openings in fiscal 2026 and opened six in Q3. It continues to target about 300 domestic Cheesecake Factory restaurants over time, and new-restaurant development is its top long-term capital priority.
quotes: We continue to target approximately 300 Company-owned and operated The Cheesecake Factory restaurants domestically over time.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A; the concentration conclusion is inferred
competitive_position.claim: The Cheesecake Factory concept is the dominant revenue source. Its fiscal 2025 sales were $2,688.8 million of $3,751.8 million total revenues, so the company depends on one flagship brand.

Differentiation rests partly on desserts and an integrated bakery. Desserts were about 17% of Cheesecake Factory sales in fiscal 2025, and the company says owning bakery production gives control over quality and is more profitable than buying from a third party.
quotes: Integration of this vital part of our brand gives us control over the creativity and quality of our desserts and is also more profitable than buying from a third party.
Our brand identity and reputation for offering premium desserts results in a significant level of dessert sales, representing approximately 17% of The Cheesecake Factory sales during fiscal 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K and the company presentation; not verified
competitive_position.claim: Off-premise sales were about 21% of Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales in fiscal 2025. The October 2026 investor presentation says the company has the highest off-premise average weekly sales among the peers it charts, but this is a management presentation.
quotes: LEVERAGING OUR DIFFERENTIATED POSITIONING TO DRIVE THE HIGHEST OFF-PREMISE AVERAGE WEEKLY SALES

competitive_position.claim: Fiscal 2025 showed weaker underlying demand than 2026. Cheesecake Factory comparable sales rose only 0.1% because a 2.4% higher average check was offset by 2.3% lower traffic. North Italia comparable sales fell about 2% on 5% lower traffic.
quotes: partially offset by decreased customer traffic of 2.3%.
North Italia comparable sales decreased approximately 2% from fiscal 2024.

competitive_position.claim: The company names competition and value perception as a threat. It competes with national and regional casual dining chains, independents, fast casual, quick-service, grocery stores and meal kits, and says traffic could suffer if rivals offer higher perceived value.
quotes: We believe that many consumers remain focused on value and if our competitors promote and deliver a higher degree of perceived value, our customer traffic could suffer.

competitive_position.claim: The company names labor and cost inflation as a threat. It says its from-scratch menu requires more labor per restaurant than rivals that use processed foods or commissaries, so wage increases could affect it more than others.
quotes: Increased restaurant labor costs could impact us more than others in our industry because we have a complex menu made fresh from scratch at our restaurants, requiring more labor at each restaurant location than some of our competitors who use processed foods or commissaries to prepare their foods.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors; no data on actual impact is given
competitive_position.claim: The company names shifting consumer preferences as a threat, including health-related changes such as GLP-1 treatments, plus the risk that less-established concepts do not reach target returns.
quotes: New and current medical treatments such as GLP-1 agonists may shift consumer preferences.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the balance sheet and 10-Q risk factor; the link to flexibility is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Financing is a named constraint. Current portion of long-term debt was 563,713 (table in thousands) at Sep. 29, 2026 versus 68,815 at Dec. 30, 2025, against cash of 249,269. The 2030 Notes are convertible during the quarter ending December 29, 2026, and conversions will be settled partly or wholly in cash.
quotes: All conversions of the 2030 Notes will be settled partially or entirely in cash.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the funding conclusion is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Operating cash flow for nine months was 313,738 (table in thousands) versus 226,374 a year earlier. This covered additions to property and equipment of 144,238, so growth capex was funded internally in the period.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 8-K; the competitive relevance is inferred from the 10-K
competitive_position.claim: A leadership transition is under way in the bakery, which the company treats as a differentiator. The president of the bakery subsidiary is retiring after 30 years and will stay into the first quarter of 2027.
quotes: Mr. Carango will continue to serve as President of the bakery into the first quarter of 2027 to assist with the leadership transition.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet [F1]. The counter point is stated in the 10-K MD&A [P3].
financial_health.claim: Cash and cash equivalents were 249,269 (table in thousands) at Sep. 29, 2026, up from 215,729 at Dec. 30, 2025. Total current assets were 469,080 against total current liabilities of 1,318,709, so current liabilities are well above current assets.

financial_health.basis: Inferred from the balance-sheet layout and from the filing's total-liabilities lines, which are consistent with no long-term debt at Sep. 29, 2026 [F1], and from the convertible-note disclosure [P5].
financial_health.claim: The current portion of long-term debt was 563,713 (table in thousands) at Sep. 29, 2026, against 68,815 at Dec. 30, 2025. The Long-term debt line shows a single figure of 561,259, which appears to be the Dec. 30, 2025 value, so no non-current debt appears to remain at Sep. 29, 2026.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the balance sheet [F1]. The lease-capacity point is stated in the 10-K MD&A [P3].
financial_health.claim: Leverage includes large lease obligations. Operating lease liabilities were 177,084 current and 1,404,351 noncurrent (table in thousands). Total liabilities were 2,875,344 against stockholders' equity of 574,066, which was up from 436,427.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement [F3] and income statement [F2]. The opening plan is stated in the earnings release [P6].
financial_health.claim: Cash provided by operating activities for the nine months was 313,738 (table in thousands), against 226,374 a year earlier. Additions to property and equipment were 144,238 against 121,048. Net income for the nine months was 179,242.

financial_health.basis: Line items are stated in the cash flow statement [F3]. The reversal point is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow exceeded net income partly because of non-cash charges and working-capital inflows. Depreciation and amortization was 86,262 and stock-based compensation was 22,810. Other accrued expenses added 64,360 and receivables added 35,724, partly offset by a 36,469 outflow from gift card liabilities (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Quoted from the earnings release [P6] and shown in the income statement [F2]. The point that the credit is non-cash is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Reported earnings for the third quarter were helped by acquisition-related income. The income statement shows acquisition-related contingent consideration, compensation and amortization income of (12,889) for the quarter (table in thousands). The company reported adjusted net income of $52.3 million against GAAP net income of $61.3 million.
quotes: The Company recorded a pre-tax net income of $12.9 million related to Fox Restaurant Concepts (“FRC”) acquisition-related items.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement [F3]. The dividend declaration is stated in the 8-K [P8].
financial_health.claim: Financing outflows in the nine months included 68,992 (table in thousands) to repay convertible debt, 44,117 of common stock dividends and 31,801 of treasury stock purchases. Treasury purchases were 142,722 in the prior-year period. Interest paid was 12,596 and income taxes paid were 22,567.

The main near-term refinancing issue is the 2030 Notes. They are convertible by holders during the fiscal quarter ending December 29, 2026, because the share price exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the required trading days.
quotes: In addition, because the last reported sale price per share of our common stock exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the 2030 Notes for at least 20 trading days during the 30 consecutive trading days ending on, and including, September 29, 2026, the 2030 Notes are convertible by holders at their option during the fiscal quarter ending December 29, 2026.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the risk factor [P5]. The sources of cash are shown in [F1] and [F3].
financial_health.claim: Conversions of the 2030 Notes will be settled partially or entirely in cash, so conversions could draw on cash. The company says it may lack enough cash or be unable to obtain financing when required.
quotes: All conversions of the 2030 Notes will be settled partially or entirely in cash.
We may not have enough available cash or be able to obtain financing at the time we are required to repurchase the 2030 Notes or pay the cash amounts due upon conversion.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q risk factor [P5]. The ratio thresholds are paraphrased from the cited text.
financial_health.claim: The Loan Agreement limits how the notes can be met. Cash paid on conversion cannot exceed the principal converted plus any bond hedge proceeds. A fundamental-change repurchase is allowed only if no default exists and the net adjusted leverage ratio is at most 4.25 to 1.00 and the EBITDAR to interest and rental expense ratio is at least 1.90 to 1.00.
quotes: For example, the Loan Agreement restricts us from paying cash upon conversion of the 2030 Notes in an amount that exceeds the sum of (i) the principal amount being converted and (ii) any payments received by us or any of our subsidiaries pursuant to the exercise, settlement or termination of any related permitted bond hedge transaction.

financial_health.basis: The repurchase is stated in the 10-K [P3]. The repayment is stated in [F3]. The link between the repayment and the 2026 Notes is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The earlier convertible notes are being paid down. A 2025 repurchase of about $276.0 million principal of the 2026 Notes cost $289.8 million including a premium. Another 68,992 (table in thousands) was repaid in the nine months to Sep. 29, 2026, and the current portion of debt at Dec. 30, 2025 was 68,815.
quotes: On February 28, 2025, we repurchased approximately $276.0 million aggregate principal amount of the 2026 Notes (as defined below) for aggregate consideration of $289.8 million, which included a premium of $13.8 million.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited releases; the conditions for continuation are inferred from management's own attribution.
growth_thesis.claim: Comparable sales at The Cheesecake Factory concept are the main recent driver of revenue growth. They rose 15.2% in Q3 fiscal 2026 after 5.8% in Q2. Q3 revenues were 1,033,440 against 907,226 a year earlier (table in thousands). For this to continue, traffic and check gains tied to menu innovation, the rewards program and social media engagement must hold.
quotes: Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
Continued menu innovation, our rewards program and significant engagement across social media contributed to the impressive sales growth

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K, 10-Q and earnings release; the conditions are stated in the 10-K and partly inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: New restaurant openings are the second stated driver. The company opened six restaurants in Q3 and still expects as many as 26 in fiscal 2026. The restaurant count was 384, against 368 at February 23, 2026. For this to continue, sites, leases, permits and staffing must be available, and the company must fund the build-out. Nine-month additions to property and equipment were 144,238 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and increases in comparable restaurant sales.
The Company continues to expect to open as many as 26 new restaurants in fiscal 2026

growth_thesis.basis: Cost percentages and the management quote are stated in the release; the mechanism is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Margin leverage is lifting profit faster than sales. Q3 food and beverage costs were 21.2% of revenues against 21.8%, and labor was 34.8% against 35.6%. Income from operations was 74,873 against 37,269 (table in thousands). For this to continue, labor productivity and food efficiency must hold and sales must stay high relative to the cost base.
quotes: year-over-year improvements in labor productivity and food efficiency supported strong profitability

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the investor presentation; the continuation conditions are drawn from the risk factor.
growth_thesis.claim: Flower Child and the other newer concepts are a further growth lever. Flower Child sales rose 27.8% in fiscal 2025, its comparable sales rose about 5%, and the company targets about 20% average annual unit growth. For this to continue, new units must be accepted in their markets and reach targeted returns.
quotes: Flower Child comparable sales increased approximately 5% from fiscal 2024.
Targeting ~20% average annual unit growth
we can provide no assurance that new restaurants will be accepted in the markets targeted for expansion or that we will be able to achieve our targeted returns when opening new locations

growth_thesis.basis: Balance sheet and cash flow figures are stated; the link to funding growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Funding capacity is a condition for continued growth. Nine-month operating cash flow was 313,738 against capex of 144,238 (table in thousands). The current portion of long-term debt was 563,713, because the 2030 Notes are convertible in the quarter ending December 29, 2026 and conversions will be settled partially or entirely in cash. Self-funded expansion therefore depends on cash generation and on meeting these obligations.
quotes: All conversions of the 2030 Notes will be settled partially or entirely in cash.

material_events.basis: Stated in the cited 10-Q risk factor update.
material_events.claim: The conversion condition for the 2030 convertible notes was met: the stock price exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the required trading days. Holders may therefore convert the notes at their option during the quarter ending December 29, 2026.
quotes: the 2030 Notes are convertible by holders at their option during the fiscal quarter ending December 29, 2026

material_events.claim: The Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.30 per share, payable November 24, 2026 to holders of record on November 10, 2026.
quotes: On October 21, 2026, the Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.30 per share which will be paid on November 24, 2026

material_events.claim: The President of the bakery subsidiary notified the company of his decision to retire. He will stay in the role into the first quarter of 2027 to assist with the leadership transition.
quotes: Keith T. Carango notified The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated
Mr. Carango will continue to serve as President of the bakery into the first quarter of 2027 to assist with the leadership transition.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-Q risk factor (P5) and the balance sheet (F1). The link between the debt reclassification and the 2030 Notes is inferred.
risks.claim: Debt due within a year jumped to $563,713 (table in thousands) from $68,815, and the 2030 Notes are convertible during the quarter ending December 29, 2026, with conversions settled partly or fully in cash. Cash was $249,269 (table in thousands) at September 29, 2026.
quotes: All conversions of the 2030 Notes will be settled partially or entirely in cash.
We may not have enough available cash or be able to obtain financing at the time we are required to repurchase the 2030 Notes or pay the cash amounts due upon conversion.

risks.basis: The comparable sales figures are stated. That they may not persist is inferred from the contrast between periods. The evidence gives no forward comparable sales guidance.
risks.claim: The Q3 fiscal 2026 comparable sales gain at The Cheesecake Factory (15.2%) is far above Q2 (5.8%) and the fiscal 2025 full-year figure (0.1%). If the surge reflects momentum from the rewards program and social media, it could fade and weaken the growth and margin story.
quotes: Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 5.8% year-over-year in the second quarter of fiscal 2026.
The Cheesecake Factory comparable sales increased by 0.1%, or $2.2 million, from fiscal 2024.

risks.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6) and in the income statement line for acquisition-related items (F2). The characterization as flattering is inferred.
risks.claim: Q3 GAAP earnings were flattered by FRC acquisition-related income. Net income was $61.3 million and diluted EPS $1.19, but adjusted net income was $52.3 million and adjusted EPS $1.02. GAAP profit may therefore overstate the ongoing run-rate.
quotes: The Company recorded a pre-tax net income of $12.9 million related to Fox Restaurant Concepts (“FRC”) acquisition-related items.

risks.basis: The figures and the opening plan are stated. The risk to returns is inferred from the 10-K discussion of new-unit inefficiencies and from the North Italia comparable sales decline.
risks.claim: Rapid unit growth, with as many as 26 new restaurants expected in fiscal 2026, raises preopening costs and execution risk, particularly at newer concepts. North Italia comparable sales fell about 2% in fiscal 2025. Q3 preopening costs were 11,160 (table in thousands) versus 6,584.
quotes: The Company continues to expect to open as many as 26 new restaurants in fiscal 2026
North Italia comparable sales decreased approximately 2% from fiscal 2024.

unresolved_questions.basis: Convertibility and cash settlement are stated in P5. The link between the 563,713 current debt and the 2030 Notes is inferred from the line item and P5, because the debt note is not in the packet.
unresolved_questions.claim: How much cash will the company have to pay out if holders convert the 2030 Notes, and how will it fund that? The balance sheet shows current debt rising sharply while cash is modest.
quotes: All conversions of the 2030 Notes will be settled partially or entirely in cash.
We may not have enough available cash or be able to obtain financing at the time we are required to repurchase the 2030 Notes or pay the cash amounts due upon conversion.

unresolved_questions.basis: The share counts are stated in F2 (shares in thousands). The dilution mechanism is inferred, because the conversion terms are not in the cited items.
unresolved_questions.claim: How many shares could be issued, and how large is the dilution, when the 2030 Notes convert? The conversion price and hedge terms are not in the packet.
quotes: the last reported sale price per share of our common stock exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the 2030 Notes for at least 20 trading days

unresolved_questions.basis: Comp rates are stated in the releases. The persistence question is inferred from the size of the change between quarters.
unresolved_questions.claim: Is the jump in The Cheesecake Factory comparable sales lasting, and how much of it came from traffic rather than price? The packet shows only the headline rates.
quotes: Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 5.8% year-over-year in the second quarter of fiscal 2026.

unresolved_questions.basis: The amounts are stated in F2 and P6. The driver of the Q3 income is not stated in the cited items. The fair-value inputs are described in P3 only for the prior year.
unresolved_questions.claim: What caused the third-quarter income from FRC acquisition-related items, and could it reverse? It lifted GAAP results above adjusted results.
quotes: The Company recorded a pre-tax net income of $12.9 million related to Fox Restaurant Concepts (“FRC”) acquisition-related items.

unresolved_questions.basis: The July target is stated in P9. Any October update is not visible in the packet, so the question is inferred from the omitted guidance text.
unresolved_questions.claim: What is the current full-year net income margin target after the Q3 results? The only target in the packet is from July and the Q3 guidance text was cut off.
quotes: to correct a typographical error on slide 31 where the fiscal year 2026 net income margin target was reported as 5% instead of 5.4%.

unresolved_questions.basis: The cash flow figures are stated in F3. The link between buyback pace and note conversions is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will share repurchases resume at the earlier pace, given the cash needs of the pending note conversions and Loan Agreement limits? Nine-month buybacks were far below the prior year.
quotes: Future decisions to pay, increase or decrease dividends or to repurchase shares are at the discretion of the Board and will be dependent on a number of factors, including limitations pursuant to the terms and conditions of our Loan Agreement and applicable law.

unresolved_questions.basis: The retirement is stated in P7. The effect on operations is not addressed in the cited items.
unresolved_questions.claim: Who will succeed the bakery subsidiary's retiring president, and does the leadership change affect bakery operations? The filing gives only the retirement and a transition period.
quotes: Mr. Carango will continue to serve as President of the bakery into the first quarter of 2027 to assist with the leadership transition.
